question.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $v$ and $w$ are orthogonal. Find $(u+9v)\cdot w+v\cdot (u+7w).$
question.worked_solution:
Since $v$ and $w$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $v\cdot w=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(u+9v)\cdot w+v\cdot (u+7w) & =u\cdot w+(9v)\cdot w+v\cdot u+v\cdot (7w) \\  & =u\cdot w+9(v\cdot w)+v\cdot u+7(v\cdot w) \\  & =u\cdot w+9\cdot 0+v\cdot u+7\cdot 0 \\  & =u\cdot w+v\cdot u \\  & =(4\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-5)+1\cdot 7+(-3)\cdot (-3)) \\  & +((-4)\cdot 4+3\cdot (-2)+5\cdot 1+4\cdot (-3)) \\  & =(8+10+7+9)+(-16-6+5-12) \\  & =34-29 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
